item.title: Lagos renews campaign against open defecation
item.description: …Calls for improved sanitation, gender-sensitive toilet facilities By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has renewed its campaign for improved sanitation, proper hygiene practices and access to safe toilet facilities as part of efforts to eliminate open defecation and promote public health. The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Akodu, and the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Tajudeen Gaji, made the call on Friday as the state joined the rest of the world to commemorate World Toilet Day at Alausa, Ikeja. The 2026 celebration was held under the theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality.” Akodu said women and girls required toilet facilities that guaranteed adequate privacy, reliable water supply, handwashing stations and hygienic conditions. He noted that Lagos’ growing population, rapid urbanisation and expanding commercial activities had placed enormous pressure on existing sanitation infrastructure. According to him, addressing the challenges requires deliberate public policies, sustained capital investment, institutional discipline and collective civic responsibility. He said the state government recognised that a clean, resilient and sustainable environment must guarantee every resident access to safe, dignified and functional sanitation facilities. Earlier, Gaji, who was represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Hassan Sanuth, said the commemoration underscored the importance of proper sanitation in preventing diseases, protecting public health and promoting a cleaner environment. He described access to safe toilets as more than a basic necessity, saying it was fundamental to human dignity and public health. Gaji said sanitation was closely linked to personal security, social equality and the fundamental right of every citizen to live in a healthy environment. He warned that inadequate access to safe and private toilet facilities could undermine people’s health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. The permanent secretary therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that would address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. The post Lagos renews campaign against open defecation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA acting MD unveils 60-day action plan
item.description: …Warns staff against laxity, promises operational overhaul By Olasunkanmi Akoni The newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to tackle waste management challenges across Lagos State, warning staff against indiscipline and poor performance. Akinyemi, who has assumed office amid growing concerns over waste accumulation across the metropolis, said the plan was aimed at clearing waste backlogs, strengthening regulatory enforcement and restoring the agency’s operational efficiency. He disclosed this on Friday while addressing management and staff at a workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa, Lagos. Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Kunle Adebiyi, the acting managing director called for renewed commitment, discipline and professionalism among workers. He said repositioning the agency would require active participation and dedication from personnel at all levels. “We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. “We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi said. Outlining the 60-day action plan, he said personnel would be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with the respective areas to strengthen field monitoring and improve response times. He also announced plans to establish decentralised operational hubs to improve supervision, facilitate faster interventions and address waste disposal blackspots across the state. On indiscriminate waste disposal, Akinyemi said the agency would intensify public enlightenment on waste sorting at source and responsible disposal practices. He said traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations and artisans would be mobilised to promote compliance with proper waste management practices. The acting managing director also called for stronger collaboration with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and urged residents to comply with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain service delivery. On staff welfare, Akinyemi assured workers that their well-being remained a priority, disclosing that efforts were underway to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered buses to address transportation challenges. Earlier, Tijani called for urgent action to revitalise LAWMA’s operational framework, saying the agency needed an immediate overhaul to improve field performance. Similarly, Adebiyi said the success of the 60-day plan would depend on prudent financial management, accountability and effective collaboration across the agency’s directorates. item.title: Nwobodo urges ESUT to prioritise innovation, research, good governance
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—-Former Governor of old Anambra State and former Minister of Sports, Chief (Dr.) Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo, has urged the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) to prioritise research, technological innovation, entrepreneurship and good governance to enhance its contribution to national development. Nwobodo made the call while delivering the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of ESUT during the university’s Special Convocation Ceremony at its permanent site at Ebe-ano City, Enugu State. The lecture was titled, “From Vision to Legacy: Technology, Education, Leadership, Good Governance and the Responsibility of a New Generation.” Nwobodo, who founded the Anambra State University of Science and Technology (ASUTECH) in 1980, said the establishment of the institution was a deliberate investment in the future, driven by the conviction that education, scientific knowledge, technological competence and visionary leadership were essential to societal progress. He expressed satisfaction with the growth of the university, noting that the institution’s continued development more than four decades after its establishment demonstrated the enduring value of its founding vision. According to him, the true measure of leadership goes beyond achievements recorded while in office to include the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations. Reflecting on his experience in public service, Nwobodo said governments and political office holders might come and go, but institutions founded on sound principles and sustained through responsible governance could endure for generations. He stressed that visionary leadership required the courage to make difficult decisions and undertake initiatives whose benefits might extend beyond one’s tenure in public office. On the future of ESUT, the former governor called for its transformation into a leading centre for research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technological development and practical solutions to societal challenges. He said the university’s success should not be measured solely by student enrolment and graduation figures but also by the quality of its research, technological discoveries, entrepreneurial achievements and contributions to national development. Nwobodo advocated increased investment in applied research, urging engineering students to develop solutions to energy and infrastructure challenges, agricultural scientists to improve food production, medical researchers to advance healthcare, and computer scientists to develop applications in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital technology. He also called for stronger collaboration among students of management, law, economics and social sciences and their counterparts in science and engineering to translate research findings into commercially viable enterprises. item.title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
item.description: By Dickson Omobola African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected. Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment. He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education. He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.” He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement. He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.” Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited. Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates. He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.” Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year. He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country. The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad. “Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said. He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems. Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital. He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority. The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment. item.title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
item.description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained. The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa. “I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria. “Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added. On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency. Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option. Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters. He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence. “First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added. Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”. The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow. Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.” The post Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: [VIDEO] I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2. item.title: Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO
item.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday. The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday. The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said that the incident was not a system collapse. It said that the disturbance resulted from the tripping of some transmission line, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”NISO wishes to clarify that the grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse. “It resulted from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country. ”At 12:34 p.m., the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex. ”Subsequently, at 12:50 p.m, the Ihovbor–Oshogbo transmission line tripped alongside the Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in load losses in some parts of the country,” it said. The system operator said that prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilize the grid and restore affected transmission lines. It said that all the affected lines had since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49 p.m. on Friday. It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations, and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid. ”The public is advised to rely on official communications from NISO for accurate information on developments within the national electricity grid,” it said. (NAN) The post Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Afenifere demands prosecution of sponsors of campaign violence
item.description: …Raises alarm over rising attacks ahead of 2027 elections By Adeola Badru The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has raised the alarm over increasing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling for the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators and their sponsors. The organisation warned that the growing incidents of thuggery, intimidation and inflammatory political rhetoric posed a serious threat to the country’s democratic process. Afenifere, in a statement issued on Friday by its National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, called on political parties, candidates, their sponsors and supporters to end violence and ensure that campaigns were conducted in accordance with the Constitution and the Electoral Act. Ajayi expressed concern over reported attacks on political figures, campaign convoys and supporters in different parts of the country, warning that the growing atmosphere of hostility could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and endanger lives. Among the incidents cited was the reported attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu on Friday, November 13, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Central Mosque, Abuja. According to the organisation, assailants threw stones and other dangerous objects at the departing presidential convoy, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives. Afenifere also condemned the attack on supporters of the Accord Party governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, around the Molete area of Ibadan, which reportedly resulted in the death of a 40-year-old supporter, Azeez Tajudeen. It described the incident as particularly disturbing, saying the destruction of vehicles and loss of life highlighted the consequences of allowing political differences to degenerate into violence. The organisation further listed the reported attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State; the reported assault on the convoy of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Calabar, Cross River State; and disruptions of political gatherings, particularly those of the APC and ADC in Sokoto, Kebbi and Lagos states. It said the incidents reflected a disturbing pattern requiring urgent intervention by political leaders and security agencies. Ajayi also recalled the warning by former President Goodluck Jonathan at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Peace Conference in Abuja, where he cautioned political leaders against running their parties like rival cult groups. Jonathan had warned against recruiting and exploiting young Nigerians for political violence, saying such practices could plunge the country into avoidable crises. Similarly, Senate President Godswill Akpabio had cautioned youths against allowing themselves to be used for political violence, warning that perpetrators could face serious criminal charges, including treasonable felony. item.title: Obi woos Onitsha voters, promises jobs, better services
item.description: …Says Nigeria needs energetic president By Vincent Ujumadu The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday drew a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall meeting in the commercial city. Obi began his visit with a stop at his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he told students that the institution had produced three state governors and could soon produce Nigeria’s president. The three former governors he identified were Peter Odili of Rivers State, Obi himself and Willie Obiano, who succeeded him as governor of Anambra State. Addressing the students, Obi promised to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in the 2027 general elections. His campaign train subsequently moved through Oguta Road, Upper Iweka, Head Bridge, Uga Road and Modebe Avenue before arriving at All Saints Cathedral, venue of the town hall meeting. Among those who accompanied him during the roadshow were Aisha Yesufu and other members of his campaign team. Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign music, while several traders reportedly closed their shops to attend the town hall meeting. Addressing supporters at the gathering, Obi said he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, had formed a team committed to uniting the country, tackling insecurity and corruption, and ensuring that public resources were used for the benefit of Nigerians. “Kwankwaso and I have formed a team that will unite and secure Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, fight corruption and use public money for public good. “I assure Nigerians that from day one, they will be feeling the good impact of their country. You will know that a new team is in charge,” he said. He promised to move Nigeria from a consumption-driven economy to one centred on production, create employment opportunities and invest in critical sectors. “We cannot continue with the present situation where our children don’t have jobs because that is not the way a country should be,” he said. On healthcare, Obi advocated a system where Nigerians could access functional medical facilities without having to depend on religious institutions for treatment. He pledged to establish functional primary healthcare centres in every ward and said his proposed administration would build 10,000 healthcare centres across the country. He also promised that his administration would commence the construction of 40,000 classroom blocks from its first day in office, alongside increased investment in education and healthcare. On electricity, the former Anambra governor expressed concern over Nigeria’s power generation capacity, which he put at about 5,000 megawatts. item.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
item.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. item.title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
item.description: …Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said. item.title: ‘I won’t disappoint you in my second term’ – Adeleke assures Osun people
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration. A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying. Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy. According to him, the Osun election that re-elected Governor Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it. “That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people,” he submitted on behalf of the Chief Imam of Osogboland, Sheikh Musa Animasahun. The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Hon. Teslim Igbalaye; Osun Central Accord Senatorial candidate, Hon. item.title: UNICEF, Lagos raise alarm over threats to children’s rights
item.description: …As children demand free education, protection, greater say in policies By Chioma Obinna The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have called for stronger protection of children’s rights, warning that their welfare and fundamental rights are increasingly under threat and require concrete government action. The call was made on Friday during the commemoration of the 2026 World Children’s Day at the UNICEF Lagos Office, with the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.” UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, said children’s rights were facing growing threats globally, stressing the need for governments and other stakeholders to guarantee every child access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to all, particularly the most vulnerable. She emphasised the importance of social protection programmes, noting that the existence of rights did not automatically translate into access to basic necessities. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said, explaining that social protection interventions could help vulnerable children access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. She added that Nigeria’s future depended largely on the attention and investment devoted to children today. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” Lafoucriere declared. The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that it could not achieve the objective without the support of other stakeholders. He urged parents, schools, communities, development partners and other stakeholders to work together to create an environment where every child felt safe, valued and heard. “We must translate what we hear today into meaningful action and commitment,” he said. Ogunlende assured the children that their contributions and concerns raised during the celebration would not end with the event but would inform government policies and practical interventions. Also speaking, the Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their lives, insisting that their voices must be considered in the formulation of policies concerning them. He said children were better positioned to communicate their experiences, particularly in cases involving abuse and other challenges. item.title: Ooni urges FG to revive, protect textile industry
item.description: …Calls for prioritisation of Nigerian fabrics, investment in local production By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to revive and protect Nigeria’s textile industry as part of efforts to strengthen the nation’s economic growth and development. The monarch also urged textile unions to deploy all necessary measures to safeguard the industry and encourage the patronage of locally produced fabrics. Oba Ogunwusi, represented by Olori Aderonke Adeyeye, made the call on Friday at the 38th Annual National Education Conference of the National Union of Textile, Garment and Tailoring Workers of Nigeria (NUTGTWN) and the Nigeria Textile, Garment and Tailoring Employers’ Association in Ile-Ife, Osun State. Commending the unions for organising the conference to educate their members, the monarch said an informed labour union was essential to the survival of democracy and the development of the nation. He said stakeholders must work together to restore the country’s textile industry, revive moribund mills and make locally manufactured fabrics a source of national pride. “It is important for stakeholders to protect our industry. Let us prioritise our own fabrics. Let us revive our textile mills. Let us make Made in Nigeria a badge of pride, not an apology. “We must honour labour. Every tailor, every cutter, every employer deserves dignity, fair pay and respect. Labour is not servitude; labour is nation-building. “Let us raise a new generation. Teach them craft, teach them the business, teach them discipline. Do not let this knowledge die with us,” he said. The Ooni further stressed that the survival of democracy was closely linked to economic prosperity, respect for workers and the protection of local industries. “Democracy cannot stand on empty stomachs. It cannot stand where labour is not respected. It cannot stand where industry is allowed to die. A nation that abandons its artisans abandons its future,” he added. Earlier, NUTGTWN President, Comrade Peter Godonu, urged the Federal Government to translate its commitment to industrialisation into concrete policies and investments capable of reviving the country’s struggling textile industry. Godonu said Nigeria could no longer afford to celebrate the potential of its textile sector while factories remained closed, production capacity declined and imported products continued to dominate the domestic market. He said the union would sustain its advocacy for policies that promote industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry. “Our Union will therefore continue to intensify its advocacy and campaign for sustainable industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry. “We remain available to partner with the Federal Government, state governments, employers and other stakeholders in developing and implementing practical solutions to these challenges,” h

item.title: I’m The Most Transparent, Vilified But I Shall Be Vindicated — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will eventually be vindicated over the allegations of financial misconduct levelled against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). He also described himself as the most transparent individual. “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated,” Bello said on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday. ﻿ When asked to respond to allegations of financial mismanagement while in government, the former governor urged people in doubt to go to the state and ask questions about how resources were managed. He said he pities those who call him a thief. The former governor also described himself as a man who was blessed by God and able to meet his needs and those of his family members. Bello, who has consistently denied wrongdoing, is facing multiple cases instituted by the anti-graft agency over alleged misappropriation of public funds during his eight-year tenure as governor of the state. The EFCC Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, said in an interview with Channels Television in January 2026 that the commission had filed three cases against the former governor and fulfilled its mandate by investigating and prosecuting him. According to Olukoyede, the responsibility for determining Bello’s guilt rests with the judiciary. One of the cases involves a 16-count charge bordering on alleged criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving ₦110.4 billion. Bello, who was the governor from 2016 to 2024, is standing trial alongside two former state government officials. The Federal Government alleges that the defendants diverted state funds to acquire properties in highbrow areas of Abuja and Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Bello is also facing a separate 19-count charge involving an alleged ₦80.2 billion fraud and money laundering before the Federal High Court in Abuja. However, some prosecution witnesses have given evidence that has featured prominently in the proceedings. In February 2026, an EFCC witness, Olomotane Egoro, told the Federal High Court that Bello’s name did not appear as a beneficiary, signatory, or party to transactions involving some companies allegedly awarded local government contracts in Kogi State. Similarly, in March, another prosecution witness, Mahmoud Abdulazeez, maintained that Bello’s name was not linked to the transactions involving property documents tendered before the court. In June 2026, the 17th prosecution witness, Shehu Bala, also told the court during cross-examination that Bello was not involved in the property transactions under examination. Meanwhile, the EFCC secured a significant legal victory in August 2025 when the Court of Appeal in Lagos restored an interim forfeiture order covering 14 properties allegedly linked to the former governor. item.title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
item.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”. “I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda. Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years. A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony. A general view of someone handling coffee beans in a plantation in the Gorongosa mountain range in Gorongosa on May 20, 2022. (Photo by Alfredo Zuniga / AFP) But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known. “We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes. Agricultural Investments In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses. Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year. The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists. The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country. But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues. Experts have long called for a more diversified economy. The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”. ‘Never Imported Coffee’ At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough. “I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said. While Tekenah has leaned into her local roots, the coffee industry has also been helped by a growing sense of cosmopolitanism in Nigeria’s cities, Ali said.
